newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala to expand reach amid strong Q1 growth.
newsitem.headline: Ayala to expand reach amid strong Q1 growth.

text.p: The Philippines' biggest conglomerate, Ayala Corp, is expanding its foothold domestically as well as venturing into regional markets, company officials said on Friday.

The expansion plans were announced as Ayala reported 22 percent growth in first-quarter net income to 1.92 billion pesos ($73 million), most of which came from its real estate, banking and insurance subsidiaries.

"I'm happy to report that our consolidated net income for the first quarter of this year reached 1.92 billion pesos, a 22 percent growth as compared to the same period last year," president Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala told stockholders during their annual meeting.
However, he cautioned investors against expecting the same growth rate to be maintained throughout the year.

"Twenty-two percent is a fairly aggressive number, I doubt if we will reach that (rate) by the end of the year...But certainly I feel comfortable in stating that this year's earnings will be comfortably above last year's level," he told reporters after the meeting. He declined to give specific numbers.

Ayala Corp's managing director for strategic planning, Rufino Luis Manotok, said flagship Ayala Land Inc and financing unit Bank of the Philippine Islands each contributed 40 percent to the parent's bottom line.

Ayala Land earlier reported net income of 1.42 billion pesos on revenues of 3.21 billion pesos in the first three months of the year. BPI posted 1.45 billion pesos in net income during the same period, a 122 percent growth from the year-ago figure.

Zobel dismissed fears that Ayala Land and BPI were affected by cash-flow problems. Philipine stocks, particularly property and bank stocks, have been battered in the past few days on the belief that real estate prices were set to fall and that banks with large exposure to property loans would be hit.
Food subsidiary Pure Foods Inc reported a 12 million peso net income in the first quarter, while telecom subsidiary Globe GMCR posted a loss of about 100 million pesos, Manotok said.
The company has earmarked 30 billion pesos as capital expenditure for 1997, up 10 billion pesos from last year.
The bulk of the expenditure will be used by Ayala Land and for the recapitalisation of Globe and its insurance subsidiaries.

On Ayala Corp's international ambitions, Zobel said: "We have developed a strategic action plan to ensure continuous competitiveness and growth ... We will expand our business not only inside the country but abroad especially in the southeast Asian region."

Fernando Zobel de Ayala, chief executive of Ayala International Pte Ltd, said Ayala Corp and Ayala Land have each committed to put in $100 million worth of equity over the next five years in a new subsidiary which will scout for real estate opportunities within the region.

"We have been looking at other opportunities abroad ... We feel that for the medium and certainly the long-term, a company of our size needs to be in the international arena, and we have decided for now to concentrate on the Asia Pacific region," he said. Conversion $1 = 26.30 pesos
